chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them both), regarding

The man who says to his slave: 'I emancipate you upon the condition that I marry you to my daughter; so if you marry (another) in addition to her, or take a concubine, then upon you is one hundred dinars.' So he emancipated him upon that condition and married him (to his daughter), and he (the freed slave) either took a concubine or married (another). He (the Imam) said: For his master (the former owner), upon him (the freed slave) is his first stipulation.

key_terms.أَعْتَقْتُكَ: I emancipate you — the act of manumission (itq), freeing a slave
key_terms.تَسَرَّيْتَ: You take a concubine (tasarri) — taking a slave-woman as a concubine, a legally distinct act from marriage
key_terms.شَرْطُهُ الْأَوَّلُ: His first stipulation — the binding condition set at the moment of emancipation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on conditions set at the time of emancipation in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal case in early Islamic jurisprudence concerning the emancipation of a slave coupled with a matrimonial condition and a financial penalty clause. A slave-owner frees his slave on condition of marrying the slave to his own daughter, stipulating that if the freed slave takes an additional wife or a concubine, he owes one hundred dinars. When the freed slave violates this stipulation, the Imam rules that the original condition stands and must be fulfilled. This ruling affirms the binding nature of conditions set at the time of emancipation (manumission), a topic extensively treated in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Al Aa’la Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) regarding

the man who is saying to his slave, ‘I will emancipate you upon (the condition) if you marry my daughter. So if you were to marry (another one) upon her, or keep a concubine, so upon you would be one hundred Dinars’. So he emancipated him upon that, and got him married (to his daughter). So if he keeps a concubine or marries (another woman)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For his master, upon him is his first condition’.
